js.shareText: Before a text goes to AI: send it as is, mask it, or keep it in-house? A 15-minute interactive guide on personal data and AI:
texts: Ask for title ideas for the Q3 sales presentation
No personal data, it can go as is.
Customer Ayşe Yılmaz, 0532 111 22 33, complains her parcel is late; draft a reply
The name and phone number are not needed for the reply. Mask them and the draft still works.
An employee’s sick-leave length and diagnosis: a slipped disc; plan the leave
Health data is special-category personal data. Keep it in-house.
Company notice: the office closes at 3pm on Friday; fix the wording
A customer’s IBAN and three months of account activity; summarise it
Banking secrecy and financial data. It does not leave the company.
Meeting note: Mehmet approved the budget, Zeynep will prepare the deck; make an action list
Mask the names and put them back when the list returns.
maskLesson: No masking: six pieces of personal data go out as they are.
Rules catch fixed formats exactly: ID, phone, email, IBAN. They miss the name and the address.
A model also catches free wording: names, addresses. It is sometimes wrong, so it gets measured.
Together: fixed formats to the rules, the rest to the model. Most real systems work this way.
js.recLesson: With these settings about {n} pieces of personal data get through unmasked every month. A high percentage is not small once it meets volume.
